target_audience_note: "An insurance policy with a choice of options intended to preserve the assets of the company." The document also requires that "the main place of business of the insurance policyholder is established in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg" for civil liability cover.
summary: Insurance product information document (IPID) for the Company Multi-risk Insurance sold under the product name Business by Baloise Assurances Luxembourg S.A. It insures the building, the content (equipment, goods or other) and civil liability, against a long list of insurable risks running from fire, storms, water damage, theft and glass breakage to loss of operation, electronic risks, machine breakage, transport and assistance, together with operational civil liability, civil liability after delivery, existing and consigned objects, accidental pollution and legal expenses cover. Material damage and civil liability extensions or packs are available as options. Coverage limits are the amounts insured mentioned in the special conditions and the document quantifies no amount.

gaps: Risk carrier: named explicitly in the header banner of both pages, "Company:  Baloise Assurances Luxembourg S.A." (the non-life entity). It is the ONLY legal entity named in the document: no claims handler, assistance provider, broker or agent appears anywhere, and the only other role mentioned is generic ("the domicile of the representative designated for this purpose", for premium payment). The schema has no carrier field, so the fact is recorded here and in key_quotes. Note the DOUBLE SPACE after "Company:" in the printed text, preserved verbatim in the quote.
Language read FROM the document, not from the tree it is filed under: the whole document is in English, headings included ("What is insured?", "Are there any exclusions of coverage?"). language=en.

edition_date: null, reference: null. No edition date, no reference code and no folio are PRINTED anywhere on the two pages (bottom 90 pt band empty on both, no text outside the page rectangle). The filename and the InDesign title in the PDF metadata read "IPID-Business-EN-LU-01-19", suggesting 01/2019, but that is not a statement of the document: not retained.

Polarity markers: the bullets are BITMAP IMAGES (1 bpc stencil masks recoloured by the graphics state), invisible to get_text AND to get_drawings. Recovered via get_text('dict'), placed by coordinate, polarity confirmed on a render: GREEN tick 7.16 x 7.94 pt at x=65.1 (covered), RED cross 7.16 x 7.22 pt at x=348.1 (not insured), ORANGE "!" 2.39 x 8.87 pt at x=350.0 (exclusion). The marker decided, not the column.

Marker arithmetic: page 1, 6 ticks + 8 crosses + 7 "!" = 21 images, equal to the image count of the layer (21); page 2, 2 ticks = the 2 items of "Where am I covered?", equal to the image count (2). Page-1 split: 6 ticks = the 6 marked items of "What is insured?"; 8 crosses = the 8 items of "What is not insured?"; 7 "!" = the 7 items of "Are there any exclusions of coverage?". The counts close exactly.

MODELLING CHOICE, declared: the document prints the insurable risks as TWO ticked bullets only (one green tick each), each of which is a long comma-separated enumeration. Those two bullets have been split into individual coverages — 22 from the first ("Fire and related dangers … assistance") and 5 from the second ("Operational civil liability … legal expenses cover") — so that each named risk is retrievable. The wording of each is the document's own; nothing was added. The authoritative marker count remains 6 ticks, not 27. Both full enumerations are also preserved verbatim in key_quotes.

The 2 optional extensions ("Material damage extensions or packs", "Civil liability extensions or packs") carry NO tick: they are introduced by a typographic dash under the sub-heading "Optional extensions:". It is that sub-heading, not a marker, that sets is_optional=true for those two. The document does not name what the packs contain.

No section inversion detected: geometric check performed. Headings at x=65.1 ("What is insured?") and x=348.1 ("What is not insured?", then "Are there any exclusions of coverage?"); no box overflows into the neighbouring column and the flat-text order matches the printed order. Negative result, reported as such.

The 15 exclusions come from TWO distinct printed boxes that the schema cannot distinguish: exclusions 1 to 8 from "What is not insured?" (red crosses), exclusions 9 to 15 from "Are there any exclusions of coverage?" (orange "!", lead-in "Damage that results:"). Printed order preserved.

Lead-in and the item that does not follow it: the exclusions box opens on "Damage that results:" and its first six items complete that sentence ("From gross negligence…", "From war…", "From a requisition…", "From explosives…", "From breach of confidence…", "From intentional…"). The SEVENTH, "Damage resulting from failure to observe best practice", does not follow the lead-in grammatically but does carry a "!" marker and is printed in the same box: it is kept as a full exclusion, with no repair of the syntax. Descriptions restore the lead-in so each item reads standalone; key_quotes remain exact slices of the text layer.

Limits: the document quantifies NO amount, NO deductible and NO percentage. The only figures in the whole document are deadlines (8 days to declare subsequent policies, 5 business days to declare an incident, 2 business days for theft) and the code-civil references 1792 and 2270. "Coverage limits: The amounts insured mentioned in the special conditions" is printed once for the whole box; it was carried into the limits field of every coverage in that box, which is a modelling choice, not a per-coverage statement.

territorial_scope: the two sentences of "Where am I covered?" are printed once, on page 2, and separate insured property (at the address of the risk) from civil liability (worldwide for operational civil liability, worldwide excluding the USA and Canada for other civil liability, subject to the main place of business being in Luxembourg). They were attached per coverage accordingly: the property/material risks carry the address sentence, the civil-liability covers carry the worldwide sentence. This attachment is an inference from the document's own two-way split, and is flagged here as such; the document does not restate the scope risk by risk.

deductibles: null - no franchise is mentioned. prescription_period: null - no prescription period is stated. definitions: empty - an IPID carries no glossary. waiting_periods: empty - no waiting period is stated.

notice_period: null. The document refers to "the notice period fixed by the law dated 27 July 1997 on insurance contracts, as amended by the law dated 7 December 2015 on the insurance sector" and to the special or general conditions, without ever quantifying a period.

target_audience = entreprises: taken from the document's own wording, "An insurance policy with a choice of options intended to preserve the assets of the company", reinforced by cover that only a legal person can hold (operational civil liability, civil liability of the corporate officers, loss of operation, and the requirement that "the main place of business of the insurance policyholder is established in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg"). The category does not come from the product type.

Text layer clean: verified free of control characters, non-breaking spaces, soft hyphens, private-use glyphs, decomposed NFD accents and line-break hyphenation. No text outside the page rectangle, no ghost header, no competing superimposed line.

Prompt text verified not truncated: independent re-extraction of both pages with page.get_text('text') via PyMuPDF, identical to the supplied text (only difference: a blank joining line inserted by the harness before the [[page 2]] marker).
